summary: BI-E4DFDCB0. Migration 20260826220000_add_mcp_oauth_authorization_server adds an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the MCP resource: three new tables (OAuthClient, OAuthAuthorizationCode, OAuthRefreshToken), one enum, and three nullable/defaulted columns on the existing McpApiToken. It collects NO new personal data. The only human identity it stores is a userId foreign key to an existing install-local User — the person who consented — which is the same subject McpApiToken already references; governance is inherited from that party record. Everything else is protocol state (token hashes, a PKCE challenge, an RFC 8707 audience URI, redirect URIs, and consented scope strings) or an operator-supplied client label. The migration is purely additive with no backfill: every pre-existing McpApiToken row keeps its meaning with a NULL oauthClientId, a NULL resource and an empty publicScopes array, so no existing row changes and no data is rewritten. All three tables are classified 'restricted' (never copied to a dev environment) because they hold or gate credentials.

fields.name: oAuthClientId
fields.reason: The public OAuth client_id. A generated dpfoc_ opaque identifier for a dynamically registered or operator-created client, or the https URL of a Client ID Metadata Document. Identifies software, never a person.
fields.provenance: Generated by this install, or the client_id URL the client presented and the AS validated against the document it fetched.

fields.name: clientName
fields.reason: Display label shown on the consent screen. Operator-entered for a pre-registered or credentials client; self-asserted by the client for a DCR registration, which is why the consent screen marks DCR clients as self-asserted rather than trusting the name.
fields.provenance: Operator input, the client's own RFC 7591 registration request, or its fetched CIMD document.

fields.name: clientSecretHash
fields.reason: SHA-256 of a confidential client's secret, used for constant-time lookup. Not reversible and not a data-subject attribute.
fields.provenance: Derived from a secret this install generated for a client_credentials client.

fields.name: clientSecretEnc
fields.reason: Encrypted copy of that secret so an operator can re-read it once. Encrypted with CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY via the existing credential-crypto helper, the same treatment McpApiToken.secretEnc already receives. A headless client's secret has to be recoverable; a short-lived access token does not, and none is stored.
fields.provenance: Generated by this install at client creation.

fields.name: ownerUserId
fields.reason: Foreign key to the existing install-local User whose authority a client_credentials client acts under. No new attribute about that person is stored — only the reference — and their platformRole still caps every call the client makes. Governance inherited from the User record.
fields.provenance: The authenticated operator who created the client.

fields.name: agentId
fields.reason: Optional foreign key to an existing Agent (coworker identity) the client acts as. Non-human identity; governance inherited from the Agent record.
fields.provenance: Operator selection at client creation.

fields.name: redirectUris
fields.reason: Registered OAuth redirect URIs, validated on every authorization request. Protocol configuration describing software endpoints, not a person.
fields.provenance: The client's registration request, its CIMD document, or operator input.

fields.name: allowedScopes
fields.reason: Public scope strings (dpf.read, dpf.work, …) capping what this client may be granted. Authorization policy, not data about a subject.
fields.provenance: Operator decision at client creation.

fields.name: metadataJson
fields.reason: The verbatim RFC 7591 registration request or fetched CIMD document, kept so an operator can audit what a client claimed about itself. Never contains a secret — the secret is hashed and encrypted in its own columns.
fields.provenance: Supplied by the registering client, or fetched by the AS from the client_id URL.

fields.name: codeHash
fields.reason: SHA-256 of a single-use authorization code that expires in minutes. Consumed atomically on first exchange so a replay is detectable.
fields.provenance: Derived from a code this install generated.

fields.name: userId
fields.reason: Foreign key to the existing User who consented. The identity of the consenting human is exactly what an authorization code must bind, and it is the same subject McpApiToken.userId already references. No new attribute is collected.
fields.provenance: The authenticated portal session that approved the consent screen.

fields.name: codeChallenge
fields.reason: RFC 7636 PKCE S256 challenge. A hash of a verifier the client keeps; the verifier itself is never stored.
fields.provenance: Supplied by the client in the authorization request.

fields.name: resource
fields.reason: RFC 8707 audience — this installation's own canonical MCP endpoint URI. Validated on every call so a token minted for one install cannot be replayed at another.
fields.provenance: This install's own origin.

fields.name: redirectUri
fields.reason: The redirect URI this code was issued against, re-checked at exchange. Typically a loopback listener on the operator's own machine.
fields.provenance: The client's authorization request, validated against its registered URIs.

fields.name: scopes
fields.reason: The public scopes the human actually approved. Authorization policy.
fields.provenance: The consent decision.

fields.name: tokenHash
fields.reason: SHA-256 of a refresh token. Rotated on every use.
fields.provenance: Derived from a token this install generated.

fields.name: userId
fields.reason: Foreign key to the existing User the token acts for. Same subject as the authorization code it descends from; no new attribute collected.
fields.provenance: The consent decision that started the chain.

fields.name: agentId
fields.reason: Optional foreign key to an existing Agent identity. Non-human; governance inherited from the Agent record.
fields.provenance: The registered client's configured agent binding.

fields.name: rotatedToId
fields.reason: Self-referencing pointer to this token's successor. It is the mechanism that makes a replayed refresh token detectable, which is why the retention window deliberately outlives the token TTL — purging the chain early would erase the evidence of a stolen token.
fields.provenance: Set by this install when the token is exchanged.

fields.name: resource
fields.reason: RFC 8707 audience, as above.
fields.provenance: This install's own origin.

fields.name: scopes
fields.reason: Public scopes carried forward from consent. A refresh may narrow this set but never widen it.
fields.provenance: The consent decision.

fields.name: oauthClientId
fields.reason: New nullable foreign key to the OAuthClient a token was issued to. NULL on every pre-existing dpfmcp_ PAT row, so no existing row changes meaning and no backfill runs. Lets revoking a client revoke what it holds.
fields.provenance: Set only when this install mints an OAuth access token.

fields.name: resource
fields.reason: New nullable RFC 8707 audience for OAuth-issued tokens. NULL on PAT rows, which are not audience-bound.
fields.provenance: This install's own origin.

fields.name: publicScopes
fields.reason: New defaulted array of the public scope strings a human consented to. Empty on every pre-existing PAT row. The granular internal grants continue to live in the existing scopes column, so the authorization gate is unchanged.
fields.provenance: The consent decision, or the operator-set allowedScopes of a client_credentials client.
